correctness.rationale: Intracluster colour repetition is an automorphism obstruction, and equal terminal supports furnish a colour-matching bisimulation. When the single terminal support contains the root support, the two components also bisimulate at matching colours. With two distinct terminal supports, the conjunction of their modal palette-reachability tests holds exactly at the root cluster. Colour minterms then isolate all vertices, so Boolean closure gives the powerset. Counting injections and distinct labelled support assignments size by size proves the product; in the single-terminal case the excluded injections are precisely those into the terminal support. Positivity and monotonicity in alphabet size give the first feasible power of two, including the zero-generator boundary. The rank-drop witness has eight two-colour generating assignments after branching and none before it; root colour 0 and the same-coloured world in the two-point terminal have identical depth-one signatures, proving sharpness. Inverting the fixed-s binomial estimate gives the stated asymptotic. VERIFICATION.md and VERIFY.py were inspected; the bounded refinement/algebra tests are corroboration, not the proof, and the uploaded program was not executed.

value.rationale: The generated subalgebra is a natural finite invariant. A uniform, exact census on labelled mixed-size branches gives sharp rank thresholds, and the explicit generator-rank decrease explains how adding a successor branch creates a separator even when it supplies no new colour. The smaller frame is not successor-closed in the larger one, so this is not a claim about surjective images of modal algebras. The witness and branching criterion justify the result beyond a routine recount of the one-terminal theorem.
